key_insight: A logarithmic correction with exponent 1/3 breaks the degeneracy between the 2D quantum-fluid energy-cascade spectrum and thermal equilibrium, enabling a positive, constant energy flux toward small scales.
engineering_relevance: The corrected spectrum improves interpretation and benchmarking of energy transfer in simulations and experiments on two-dimensional Bose gases.
method: Asymptotically expand the wave-kinetic collision integral to derive the logarithmic correction.
Set the logarithmic cutoff by the dissipation scale and regularize the infrared divergence at the forcing scale.
Test the predicted spectrum using Gross–Pitaevskii and wave-kinetic simulations.
evidence_signal: Both simulation approaches support the predicted spectral shape, while finite spectral ranges can exhibit apparent power laws steeper than the dimensional prediction.
watch_item: The spectral-prefactor estimate assumes asymptotically well-separated forcing and dissipation scales, so finite-range applications require caution.
paper_title: Energy cascade spectrum in wave turbulence of a two-dimensional quantum fluid
